analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Listen, I have the number of a really good, affordable computer repair shop at home. My dad has used this guy before and he can work miracles. Let's go back to my house and we can call the repair shop. 听着，我家里有一家很不错又实惠的电脑维修店的电话。我爸以前找过这个人，他能化腐朽 为神奇。咱们回我家，给那家维修店打个电话吧。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: Let's… 之前被否掉、之后才是定案。前文 P7 先提"在保修期就退给厂家换新机"，但 P8 一 句 The warranty ran out three days before I broke it（保修过期了）把它否掉；真正的 定案信号是 P9 里 Sarah 的建议句 Let's go back to my house and we can call the repair shop——Let's 引出的才是最终方案。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: call the repair shop ↔Call the repair shop to fix it. 打电话给维修店 = 找维修店修

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 A 盗用录音 My dad has used this guy before 里的 dad，制造"听到 dad 就选"的诱惑； 但录音只是说"她爸以前找过这家维修店"，用来佐证店靠谱，并非"向她爸求助"，故 A 偷换 概念。 借用原文：My dad has used this guy before and he can work miracles C) 与原文相反 C 盗用录音 send it back to the manufacturer 里的 manufacturer，听起来像方案之一； 但 P8 的 The warranty ran out（保修已过期）已把这条路堵死，它是被否掉的方案，非最 终决定。 借用原文：you can easily send it back to the manufacturer D) 与原文相反 D 盗用录音 they'll send you a brand-new one 里的 brand-new，最诱人；但"免费换新 机"的前提是 Is the laptop still under warranty，而保修已过期，这个方案随之作废，故 D 与原文相反。 借用原文：they'll send you a brand-new one for free surely

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Let's go back to my house and we can call the repair shop, and you can have some tea and cookies too. 咱们回我家，给那家维修店打个电话，你还可以喝点茶、吃点饼干。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: Let's / you can have 引出的主动招待。答案信号是 Sarah 结尾的邀约句 you can have some tea and cookies too——you can have 引出她要为 David 提供的招待。听对话结 尾热心一方 Let's…、you can… 的邀约动作，就是"她要做什么"的落点。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: you can have some tea and cookies too ↔Offer David some refreshments. 茶和饼干 = refreshments（茶点）

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 过度推断 A 盗用录音 all my essays are in there 的 essays，听上去像"帮他取回论文"；但 Sarah 提 供的是"打电话找维修店修电脑"，retrieve essays（取回论文）是修好后才可能的结果，录 音并未说她要去取论文，属过度推断。 借用原文：all my essays are in there B) 未提及 B 借"去她家、提到她 dad"的语境（My dad has used this guy before）让人联想"见家 长"；但录音只说回她家打电话、吃茶点，从没提"introduce David to her parents（引见 给父母）"，属无中生有。 D) 与原文相反 D 把录音 Let's go back to my house（回我家）的方向偷偷反过来，写成 Accompany David to his home.（陪他回他家）。go back to my house 指"去 Sarah 家"，与"to his home"正好相反，属方向/地点偷换。 借用原文：Let's go back to my house 1 M: Welcome to this week's episode of Book Talk. With me today is Heidi Brown, a historian who has written five critically acclaimed books about military history. M: 欢迎收看本周的《书谈》节目。今天和我一起的是 Heidi Brown,一位历史学家,她已经写了五本广受好 评的军事史著作。 2 W: Thanks for having me, John. I'm so excited to talk about my latest book, which was published last month. W: 谢谢邀请我来,John。我非常兴奋能谈谈我上个月出版的最新作品。 3 M: So this book is a novel, your first attempt at that genre. I thought it was a bit of a departure for you. M: 所以这本书是一部小说,你在这个体裁上的首次尝试。我觉得这对你来说是个不小的转变。 4 W: I'd say it's a major departure as it's not just a work of fiction. It's set 200 years in the future. W: 我会说这是一个重大转变,因为它不仅仅是一部虚构作品。它的背景设定在200年后的未来。 5 M: Right. So how did that happen? You spent three decades writing about the past and focusing on the 18th and 19th centuries. And now you're speculating about the future. M: 对。那这是怎么发生的呢?你花了三十年写关于过去的历史,专注于18和19世纪。现在你却在推测 未来。 Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 6 W: Well, after years of researching soldiers and chronicling their lives during battle, I just started wondering about other facets of their lives, especially their personal lives. W: 嗯,在多年研究士兵并记录他们在战斗中的生活之后,我开始想了解他们生活的其他方面,尤其是他们的私 人生活。 7 M: I can see that. Your novel is about soldiers and it focuses on their relationships, especially the bond between sons and mothers and men and their wives. M: 我能理解。你的小说是关于士兵的,它聚焦于他们的人际关系,尤其是儿子与母亲之间以及男人与妻子之 间的纽带。 8 W: Yes. That focus came about when I still intended to write another book of history. I started by researching soldiers' actual personal lives, studying their letters home. W: 是的。这个关注点出现的时候,我还打算写另一本历史书。我从研究士兵们真实的私人生活开始,研读他 们寄回家的信件。 9 M: So how did that history book become a novel? M: 那么那本历史书是怎么变成小说的呢? 10 W: Well, I realized that the historical record was incomplete. So I'd either have to leave a lot of gaps or make a lot more assumptions than a historian should. W: 嗯,我意识到历史记录是不完整的。所以我要么留下很多空白,要么做出比历史学家应该做的更多的 假设。 11 M: But why write a novel set in the future when your credentials are perfect for a historical novel? As a historian, any historical novel you write would have a lot of credibility. M: 但为什么要写一部设定在未来的小说呢,你的资历写历史小说是完美的。作为一位历史学家,你写的任何 历史小说都会有很高的可信度。 12 W: I felt too constrained working with the past, like what I wrote needed to be fact as opposed to fiction, but writing about the future gave me more freedom to imagine, to invent. W: 我觉得写过去的东西太受限制了,就像我写的东西需要是事实而不是虚构,但写未来给了我更多想象和创 造的自由。 13 M: Well, having read your book, I'm glad you made that choice to move into fiction. M: 嗯,读了你的书之后,我很高兴你做出了转向虚构写作的选择。

questions.stem: What does the woman say about her writing history books?
questions.stemZh: 女士对她写历史书籍说了什么?
questions.answerText: She doesn't have much freedom for imagination.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: I felt too constrained working with the past, like what I wrote needed to be fact as opposed to fiction, but writing about the future gave me more freedom to imagine, to invent. 处理过去的题材让我感到太受束缚，好像我写的东西必须是事实而不能是虚构；而写未来则 给了我更多想象、虚构的自由。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 感受词 felt too constrained + 转折 but。信号有两处：一是被问者直陈感受的 I felt too constrained working with the past（写过去让我太受束缚），二是 but writing about the future gave me more freedom 的转折 but——"过去受限 / 未来更自由" 的对比正是 答案落点；写史书（过去）即 "没有多少想象的自由"。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: I felt too constrained working with the past ↔She doesn't have much freedom for imagination. constrained=没有多少自由，肯否定转换 writing about the future gave me more freedom to imagine, to invent ↔freedom for imagination freedom to imagine=freedom for imagination

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 张冠李戴 make her readers believe in her 蹭了主持人那句 any historical novel you write would have a lot of credibility 的 credibility，但那是主持人讲 "你写历史小说会很可信"，不是她 说 "难让读者相信她"，张冠李戴且意思相反。 借用原文：any historical novel you write would have a lot of credibility C) 未提及 difficult to attract young readers 里的 "young readers" 原文从头到尾没出现，她谈的是 写作自由问题，跟 "吸引年轻读者" 毫无关系。 D) 与原文相反 combine fact with fiction 直接搬来原文的 fact as opposed to fiction，但原文是 "事实 与 虚构 相对立"，且她觉得写史书时只能要 fact 不能要 fiction，根本不是 "把事实与虚构 结合"。 借用原文：what I wrote needed to be fact as opposed to fiction Section B 1 Whether it's in the hands of animated polar bears or Santa Claus, there's one thing you'll find in nearly all ads for Coca-Cola: the characteristic glass bottle. Most Americans don't drink soda out of the glass bottles seen in Coke's ads anymore. But this week, the company is celebrating a century of the bottle that's been sold in more than 200 countries. 无论是在动画北极熊还是圣诞老人的手中,有一样东西几乎出现在所有可口可乐的广告里:那就是标志性的 玻璃瓶。如今大多数美国人不再用可口可乐广告中出现的玻璃瓶喝汽水了。但本周,这家公司正在庆祝这款 已在200多个国家销售的瓶子诞生一百周年。 2 Flash back to 1915, when a bottle of Coca-Cola cost just a nickel. As the soft drink gained in popularity, it faced a growing number of competitors—counterfeits even trying to copy Coke's logo. So, Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard. according to Coca-Cola historian Ted Ryan, the company decided to come up with packaging that couldn't be duplicated. 回到1915年,当时一瓶可口可乐只需五分钱。随着这种软饮料越来越受欢迎,它面临着越来越多的竞争对手 ——甚至有假冒产品试图模仿可口可乐的标识。因此,据可口可乐历史学家Ted Ryan称,公司决定设计出无 法被复制的包装。 3 A product request was sent to eight different glass makers. One factor hindering this is that parents can't or don't spend enough quality time with their kids, and substitute this deficit with toys, games, gadgets and the like. Rather than getting material things, children need parents' devoted attention. The quantity of time spent together is less important than the content of that time. This teaches them to value the effort as well as what it achieves. 毫无疑问，父母想要培养快乐的孩子，让他们自信、有能力、讨人喜欢，而不是被宠坏和痛苦。阻碍这一 点的一个因素是父母无法或没有花足够的优质时间陪伴孩子,并用玩具、游戏、小玩意儿等来弥补这一缺 失。孩子需要的不是物质的东西,而是父母全心全意的关注。一起度过的时间数量不如那段时间的内容重 Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard. 要。父母应该帮助孩子制定计划来赢得他们想要的东西,而不是立即满足他们的愿望。这教会他们珍惜努力 以及努力所带来的成果。 3 Allow them to enjoy anticipation. This teaches them to be understanding of and sympathetic towards others—qualities sure to take them a long way in life. 最后,父母应该鼓励孩子从其他角度看待生活,而不仅仅是他们自己的角度。这教会他们理解和同情他人 ——这些品质必将使他们在人生中走得更远。

P1 In recent years, the food industry has increased its use of labels. Whether the labels say 'non- GMO(非转基因的)' or 'no sugar,' or 'zero carbohydrates', consumers are increasingly demanding more information about what's in their food. One report found that 39 percent of consumers would switch from the brands they currently buy to others that provide clearer, more accurate product information. Food manufacturers are responding to the report with new labels to meet that demand, and they're doing so with an eye towards giving their products an advantage over the competition, and bolstering profits.

P2 This strategy makes intuitive sense. If consumers say they want transparency, tell them exactly what is in your product. That is simply supplying a certain demand. But the marketing strategy in response to this consumer demand has gone beyond articulating what is in a product, to labeling what is NOT in the food. These labels are known as "absence claims" labels, and they represent an emerging labeling trend that is detrimental both to the consumers who purchase the products and the industry that supplies them. 

P3 For example, Hunt's put a "non-GMO" label on its canned crushed tomatoes a few years ago— despite the fact that at the time there was no such thing as a GMO tomato on the market. Some dairy companies are using the "non-GMO" label on their milk, despite the fact that all milk is naturally GMO- free, another label that creates unnecessary fear around food.

P4 While creating labels that play on consumer fears and misconceptions about their food may give a company a temporary marketing advantage over competing products on the grocery aisle, in the long term this strategy will have just the opposite effect: by injecting fear into the discourse about our food, we run the risk of eroding consumer trust in not just a single product, but the entire food business.

P5 Eventually, it becomes a question in consumers' minds: Were these foods ever safe? By purchasing and consuming these types of products, have I already done some kind of harm to my family or the planet?

P6 For food manufacturers, it will mean damaged consumer trust and lower sales for everyone. And this isn't just supposition. A recent study found that absence claims labels can create a stigma around foods even when there is no scientific evidence that they cause harm.

P7 It's clear that food manufacturers must tread carefully when it comes to using absence claims. In addition to the likely negative long-term impact on sales, this verbal trick sends a message that innovations in farming and food processing are unwelcome, eventually leading to less efficiency, fewer choices for consumers, and ultimately, more costly food products. If we allow this kind of labeling to continue, we will all lose.

writing.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay related to the short passage given below. In your essay, you are to comment on the phenomenon described in the passage and suggest measures to address the issue. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. Young people spend a lot of time on the Internet. However, they are sometimes unable to recognize false information on the Internet, judge the reliability of online information sources, or tell real news stories from fake ones.
writing.model: It has become a common phenomenon that young people spend a great deal of time online, yet many of them struggle to tell trustworthy information from falsehood. As the passage notes, they are often unable to recognize false information, judge the reliability of online sources, or distinguish real news from fake stories. This deficiency in digital judgment, though easily overlooked, deserves our serious attention. The consequences are far from trivial. Misled by fabricated news, young people may form distorted views of the world, make ill-informed decisions, and even spread rumours unknowingly. Since their critical-thinking skills are still developing, they are especially vulnerable to eye-catching yet groundless claims that circulate rapidly across social media. To address this issue, concerted efforts are needed. First and foremost, schools should offer media-literacy courses that teach students how to verify facts and trace information back to its source. Meanwhile, online platforms ought to strengthen fact-checking and clearly label questionable content. Finally, young people themselves should cultivate the habit of cross-checking a story against several reliable sources before believing or sharing it. Only in this way can they navigate the digital world wisely.

sentences.text: 以"会址"为受动主语用被动主干（主语策略：转被动） 中文"会址修复""建立纪念馆""对外开放"都没有点明施事者（是谁修、谁建、谁开放），动作的承 受对象是会址。把承受者中共一大会址提作主语，主干用被动 the site was restored，后两个动作 并列接被动。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 三个动作并列为被动谓语 "修复""建立纪念馆""对外开放"是同一主语承受的三件先后发生的事，处理成并列被动谓语：was restored, ( a memorial hall was built / and turned into a memorial hall ) and opened to the public。可把"建立纪念馆"译为 turned into a memorial hall，让三动作共用一个被动主语更 紧凑。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 "1952年9月"明确是过去时间点，回指全篇基调用一般过去时：was restored, turned, opened。 语态 三个动作均无施事者、会址是被动承受者，全部用被动语态 was restored / was turned / was opened，切忌写成主动的 restored itself。 冠词 "纪念馆"首次出现的可数单数名词，用不定冠词 a memorial hall；"对外"的"外"指公众，用定冠词 搭配 to the public。 介词搭配 时间用 In September 1952；"对外开放"固定搭配 open to the public。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: In September 1952, the site of the First National Congress was restored, turned into a memorial hall, and opened to the public. 4. 纪念馆除了介绍参加一大的代表之外，还介绍党的历史发展进程，现已成为了解党史,缅怀革 命先烈的爱国主义教育基地。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: "纪念馆"作主语带两组谓语（主语策略：原句主语） 主语是纪念馆 the memorial hall。它有两层信息：一是"介绍…"（introduces…），二是"现已成 为…基地"（has become a base…）。可以"纪念馆"为统一主语分两句处理，第一句讲介绍内容， 第二句讲它今天的身份。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 让步状语与目的定语降级 "除了…之外，还…"用 In addition to introducing…, it also introduces… 的介词短语+also结构处 理除了介绍参加一大的代表之外，还介绍党的历史发展进程；"了解党史、缅怀革命先烈"是"基 地"的功能/目的，降级成 for understanding the Party's history and commemorating revolutionary martyrs 的介词短语作后置定语，挂到 base 上。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 "介绍…"是纪念馆现在持续做的事，用一般现在时 introduces；"现已成为"是"过去发生、延续到现 在"的结果，偏离全篇过去时基调，用现在完成时 has become——这是末句唯一需要换时态的地 方。 主谓一致 主语 the memorial hall 是第三人称单数，现在时谓语加 -s：introduces；现在完成时用 has become（不是 have）。 单复数 "代表"不止一位，用复数 the delegates；"革命先烈"是多位，用复数 revolutionary martyrs。 动名词搭配 In addition to 和 for 后面都接动名词：In addition to introducing… ; a base for understanding… and commemorating…，介词后动词一律 -ing。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: In addition to introducing the delegates who attended the First National Congress, the memorial hall also presents the course of the Party's historical development. It has now become a base for patriotism education, where people can learn about the Party's history and commemorate revolutionary martyrs. 英语六级 2021年12月·第1套 · 全卷构成 Part III Part III Part III Part III
